Vivek —

Quick read and summary below (high level). I marked the redline and drafted a counter paragraph (attached). Key points:

1) Output ownership: we can agree that customer owns outputs that are directly generated from their confidential input. We need to carve out derivative outputs that result from generalization of our models (i.e., outputs not tied to their confidential inputs). Proposed clause: "Customer shall retain ownership of outputs generated solely from Customer-provided Content; Redwood shall retain ownership of model weights, aggregated improvements, and outputs not reasonably attributable to Customer Content."

2) Training/data use: Seastone seeks a broad ban. We should offer a clear opt-in for training (customer elects in order form), plus an explicit statement that Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train models unless Customer opts in and provides affirmative consent. That addresses the procurement ask while preserving our ability to work with customers who opt into productization.

3) Feedback/telemetry: recommend a narrow, non-exclusive, non-identifying telemetry license for ops/quality improvements with a promise to honor deletion requests for any specific customer identifiers. We should include retention boundaries (e.g., 90 days for raw logs unless otherwise required for security incident investigation) and an audit hook.

I attached a tracked counter (redwood_proposed_countertrack.docx) with suggested edits on the redline. If Ben and Priyom sign off on the operational bullets, I think this is ready to send back as a single counter to close the loop.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Couple of operational notes from infra/ops:

- Telemetry scope: we can restrict telemetry to non-identifiable metrics (latency, token counts, error rates) by default. Any customer-configured debug logs that include PII need an explicit checkbox and will be treated as customer-provided debugging artifacts (not used for training).
- Retention: 90 days default for aggregated logs is feasible. For security investigation, we can extend retention under mutual agreement with a defined approval workflow.
- Opt-in UX: to make procurement comfortable we should include an Order Form checkbox for "Allow Redwood to use de-identified Customer Outputs and telemetry to improve models and services" with a short description and an escalation path to opt-out post-sale within 30 days.

I also flagged a minor SLA implication — if a customer insists on zero telemetry we need to scope a higher support/monitoring SLA (manual diagnostics). That should be captured in the commercial proposal.

Ben Carter
Director, Product Ops

Marta / Seastone team —

Thanks for the redline. We discussed internally and propose the following single-counter approach to accelerate:

1) Ownership: Customer owns outputs generated exclusively from Customer Content. Redwood retains ownership of model weights and outputs that cannot be reasonably tied to Customer Content (draft language attached).

2) Training: Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train models unless Customer elects to opt-in on the Order Form. Opt-in will be explicit (checkbox) and reversible; we will provide a process to request removal of Customer Content from training datasets within 30 days of request.

3) Feedback license and telemetry: Redwood seeks a narrow, non-exclusive license to use de-identified telemetry and aggregated metrics for service improvements. We propose 90 day default retention for aggregated logs, extended only for security investigations with mutual approval. We will include auditability and a contact for data deletion or additional controls.

We attached a tracked counter (redwood_proposed_countertrack.docx) reflecting the above. If this aligns we can prepare an edited MSA + Order Form and route via DocuSign.
